I think the L3 is justified, as stated in: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2142#issuecomment-2414407713

> For L1, just removing the Server: Apache/2.4.54 (Ubuntu) from the response header could be enough

L1 is meant for "1st layer of defense only" and this is clearly not the case here.

Hiding the version does not fix any vulnerability. Section text explains it:

> Many of these issues are rarely rated as a significant risk, but they are chained together with other vulnerabilities. If these issues are not present by default, it raises the bar for attacking an application.

> For example, hiding the version of server-side components does not fix the need to patch all components, and disabling the folder listing does not eliminate the need to use authorization controls or keep files away from the public folder, but it raises the bar.

L3 suits well - just hiding version information does not prevent any real attack, it just does not advertise the used version and makes it a bit harder to map the software version usage and update timelines used, and suits the category "extra steps to do".

Colleagues, it slightly of topic here, but if it goes to real cases, such leakage is not only about version, but also names of components, OS, etc. So, shall we extend [13.4.6](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x22-V13-Config.md#v134-unintended-information-leakage) to such technical information also?
For example, put 13.4.6 in following way: 

> Verify that the application does not expose detailed **technical** and version information of backend components.

@elarlang, thank you for mentioning these information leakage related requirements. And I was also thinking about them when reading the discussion above...
This is totally great that they are specific and cover the most important leakage channels related to debug mode remain enabled, excessive error info, more then needed API docs exposed, TRACE method. 
But it seems that 13.4.6 addresses another one important channel of information leakage: versions and names of backend components used: OS, Web server, frameworks used, etc. 
Usually during preparation for production it is aimed to minimize exposure of such data. E.g. in example above -- remove server info  like "Server: Apache/2.4.54 (Ubuntu)" at all (if it is possible and such information not needed by other components, including frontend). 
Also, for example, such checks also included into [OWASP WSTG](https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/stable/) (WSTG-INFO-08, WSTG-INFO-09). 

And what I am thinking about: why this L3 the requirement is **_only about versions_** of software used in backend components... 
But it is also great point in requirements above that they are specific, and I see that suggested by me wording may be too general. 
If we go with such clarification, it could be put it in more specific way:

> Verify that the application does not expose detailed information on versions and names of backend components (e.g. operating systems, Web servers, frameworks).

or

> Verify that the application does not expose excessive fingerprints of backend components, such as detailed information on versions and names of operating systems, Web servers, frameworks.
